reasons.correctness: createTicket publishes SupportTicketCreatedEvent with all six values through ApplicationEventPublisher, and the listener sends it AFTER_COMMIT. The interface names match exactly. Build is green and hidden tests pass 3/3.
reasons.convention_fit: The listener lives in the feature package support/ticket/event and uses @RequiredArgsConstructor with a private final field. It is annotated @TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT) and catches and logs failures. The agent read InvoiceCreatedEventListener before writing it.
reasons.design_fit: Reuses Spring's ApplicationEventPublisher and follows the existing subscription/event pattern. The event is a plain data carrier. The service constructor gains one parameter. The footprint is minimal with no new mechanism.
reasons.test_quality: SupportTicketCreatedEventListenerUnitTest uses MockitoExtension and covers the send path and the swallowed-failure path. No unit test verifies that SupportTicketService#createTicket publishes the event instead of calling EmailService.
reasons.graph_use: Graph queries mapped the support package and located the existing *EventListener files before any edit, which led to reading InvoiceCreatedEventListener. Later navigation fell back to grep and glob, and two reads failed on a wrong path prefix.
